items.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I think it might have been Guiliani, Rudy Guiliani, our friend, who they started to enforce a law

ctx.x: Some. I first saw it in the mid 80s around ’88, well close to 90. I used to play a lot of cabaret, like I would be house drummer in places where we would back up singers. And the city, I don’t remember who was the mayor, I think it might have been Guiliani, Rudy Guiliani, our friend, who they started to enforce a law where you cannot have a live band within a certain amount of feet from a residential area. So all of a sudden they started enforcing a law where you couldn’t have a band. So what they started to do,…
Yeah, the DJ and live performer they’ve kind of —
